title_options: You're A Baby T. rex. How Do You Survive? 🦖
facts: Funston et al. 2021, Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences: first tyrannosaur embryo/hatchling fossils (not T. rex; a related tyrannosaur), hatchlings about the size of a small dog (~0.7-0.9 m).

Schroeder et al. 2021, Science: juvenile giant theropods were light and fleet-footed and took the place of medium-sized predators; Woodward et al. 2020, Science Advances: juvenile T. rex fast and knife-toothed.
Erickson et al. 2004, Nature (corrigendum 2016): T. rex growth spurt from about age 14 to 18, peak about 2.1 kg a day (~767 kg a year); maximum age in the sample ~28 years.
description: Start life the size of a small dog, end up a giant. Here's how a young T. rex survived, step by step, from the fossils. #shorts #dinosaurs #TRex #Science
sources: Funston et al. 2021, Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences; Schroeder et al. 2021, Science; Woodward et al. 2020, Science Advances; Erickson et al. 2004, Nature (corrigendum 2016).

scenes.narration: You're a baby tyrannosaur, no bigger than a small dog.
So you don't fight. You run. Young T. rex had long, slim legs, built for speed.
But your bite can't crush bone like an adult's. So you hunt smaller, quicker animals that the giants ignore.
Then, around age fourteen, you hit a growth spurt, about two kilos heavier every single day.
Four years later, you weigh several tonnes, and nothing hunts you anymore.
So would you rather be the fast teenager, or the giant adult?
